name: push-tag-human-approved-release-only
body:
Correction folding C1 and C2 of the coordinator's amendment brief into the release-agent amendment of the in-flight `agent-builder-roster-cleanup` change-set.

C1 — the law's name. The recurring rule is **push/tag remain human-approved acts**, not "human acts". The same name must be used everywhere the law is stated — on the agent-policy surfaces (`opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and on the binary-doc surfaces (`Cargo.toml` line 20, `src/git/mod.rs` line 6, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs` line 28, `tests/git_e2e.rs` lines 952 and 972, `tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs` line 312). The correction is wording only: the binary's git2-only behaviour (`default-features = false`; the git CLI is never shelled out to) and `scripts/release.sh`'s never-pushes behaviour are unchanged. `plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md` line 71 is a historical plan record and is deliberately NOT edited.

C2 — who may push/tag, and how. Only the optional per-repo `release-agent` (see `requirements.requirement.agent-builder-optional-release-agent`) is ever granted `git push`/`git tag`, and its grant is `ask`: every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. The `codebase-navigator` additionally captures explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching it via `task`, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command. Every OTHER generated agent — the core/root `implementer`, each per-subsystem `<name>-implementer`, and each tiered `test-implementer` — gets NO push/tag grant at all: under the deny-by-default permission block the verbs are absent, hence denied. The template's current instruction to scaffold push/tag `ask` on every generated agent, and its git-conventions interview that offers push/tag as a per-agent choice, are superseded.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every listed surface states the rule as "human-approved acts" (or, for a sentence about the release-agent, states the release-agent-only + `ask` model).
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` grants `git push`/`git tag` ONLY to the optional `release-agent`, and only as `ask`; its permission-shape prose (rule 6), its step-3 git-conventions interview, and its permission-value prose no longer instruct scaffolding push/tag `ask` on every generated agent or offer push/tag as a per-agent choice.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` states the navigator obtains explicit user consent before dispatching the release-agent, and its push/tag clause says human-approved.
- `AGENTS.md` states push/tag are human-approved acts and that only the release-agent may push/tag (behind the consent gate and the per-op `ask`).
- The binary's git2-only behaviour and `scripts/release.sh`'s never-pushes behaviour are unchanged; the binary-doc edits correct the law's name, not the behaviour.
- `plans/SPEC-apg-projects.md` is not edited (historical).
- Scope is product source + the repo guide + the named binary-doc/test surfaces; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are NOT edited. No binary behaviour change, and no test-behaviour change (the two e2e edits are comment/message wording).
